derivation: Every ceiling here was measured over the composed artifact this tree produces, by scripts/artifact/check-bundle-budgets.mjs itself: run `node scripts/artifact/check-bundle-budgets.mjs --rederive` after `just prerender` to re-derive them all. Nothing in this file is a target somebody picked; it is the floor this tree reaches, so a payload cannot rise back into it silently.

An app's `entry` is every JavaScript byte its own document loads eagerly, plus every chunk reachable from those scripts through the runtime that loads them. Its `page` is the same closure for the `./Page` expose a host composes, read from the container's own expose module map. Shared chunks count inside both, so payload moved out of a chunk and into one it imports still counts against the same ceiling instead of escaping it. Only JavaScript is counted; page CSS is inlined into the composed documents and is measured by the artifact gate beside this one.

A route's ceiling is the sum of the `./Page` chunks it composes, over exactly the remotes `routeFragments` in scripts/compose/compose.mjs declares for it. Per-app ceilings alone would not have caught the regression this file exists for: seven panes each a little larger is a route several megabytes larger.

`marginPercent` is the one margin every ceiling in this file carries, so no single app or route can be given room a regression could hide in. It is bounded by what it must not absorb: a margin at or above the smallest CV domain's share of the largest budgeted `./Page` chunk would let that domain back into that chunk unnoticed. Neither of those two sizes is restated here, because either can move: scripts/artifact/bundle-budgets.spec.ts derives them — the smallest file under libs/data-access-core/vendor/codegen/domains, and the largest `./Page` measurement in this file — holds this margin under the bound they set, and then proves it by appending that domain to that chunk and requiring this gate to refuse the result.
